extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, experimental scientists, astronomers, opticians, and practical engineers (17th-century learned readers)
extracted.subtask_description: Summaries and methods for designing and reporting natural-philosophy experiments and observations across topics (cold/ice, optics, tides, mining, rock-breaking, astronomical observation). Emphasises experimental set-ups, measurement choices, and practical construction details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of thermometers not subject to atmospheric alteration
rubrics_metrics.description: Make exact discoveries of different degrees of coldness by such thermometers as are not subject to the alterations of the atmosphere's gravitation, nor to be frozen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose thermometer designs that avoid atmospheric pressure effects and freezing of the instrument itself to obtain reliable regional coldness comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safe freezing of liquids (freeze from bottom)
rubrics_metrics.description: A way of freezing liquors without danger of breaking the vessel, by making them begin to freeze at the bottom, not the top.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrange experiments so ice formation initiates at the bottom of the vessel to prevent bursting; useful for studying freezing behaviour while preserving containers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate thawing methods for organic material
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigate whether frozen apples or eggs thawed near the fire are spoiled, but if immersed in cold water the internal cold will be drawn out and bodies harmlessly thawed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare thawing by external heat versus immersion in cold water; apply observations to other bodies and even to humans suffering from extreme cold, and document outcomes (spoilage, preservation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Test effect of intense cold on material properties
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine whether iron, other metals, glass, stone, cheese, etc., exposed to freezing air, snow, or salt, when immersed in water will produce any ice, and whether freezing/thawing alters medicinal virtues or electrical/magnetic faculties (amber, loadstones).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design post-freeze tests of chemical, medicinal, electrical, and magnetic properties to determine impairment or alteration due to intense cold; include controlled comparisons with unfrozen samples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure which bodies expand upon freezing and cause of expansion
rubrics_metrics.description: What bodies are expanded by being frozen, and how that expansion is evinced; and whether it is caused by the intrusion of air; and whether what is contained in icy bubbles is true and elastic air.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document experiments showing expansion (or lack thereof), test for trapped air in ice bubbles, and consider alternative explanations (e.g., intrusion of air) with direct measurements and observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure which bodies contract with cold
rubrics_metrics.description: What bodies they are, that are contracted by cold; and how that contraction is evinced (including whether chemical oils by congealation behave like expressed oils or like aqueous liquors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare contraction across different classes of liquids (oils vs aqueous) and provide experimental evidence of dimensional change on cooling/congealing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantify expansion/contraction of liquids by cold
rubrics_metrics.description: What are the ways of measuring the quantity of the expansion and contraction of liquors by cold, and how the author's account agrees with navigators' observations touching pieces of ice and their apparent depths/heights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use measurement methods to quantify volumetric change and reconcile laboratory measurements with field reports (e.g., seamen observing ice heights).

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimate expansive force of freezing water
rubrics_metrics.description: How strong the expansion of freezing water is; enumerate vessel types that burst when filled with water and exposed to cold, and express the weight that can be removed by the expansive force of freezing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct experiments to determine forces generated during freezing, list which containers fail, attempt to attribute causes (compare hypotheses such as Cartesian or Epicurean).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine sphere of activity of cold and diffusion limits
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the sphere of activity of cold, or the space to whose extremities the action of a cold body is able to reach; with experiments to examine diffusion through various media, including apparently void spaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully design experiments to determine range of cold action, avoid using media of excessive thickness (which can obscure diffusion), test through metal vessels, test possible action through vacua or through media actually hot (i.e. opposing heat sources).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overly-thick media when testing diffusion
rubrics_metrics.description: When examining whether cold may be diffused through all mediums indefinitely, do not make trials with mediums of too great thickness; otherwise tests may be inconclusive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sufficiently thin barriers/media when attempting to detect diffusion of cold; include positive-control setups (e.g., metallic vessels, icy cups) to confirm transmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimate mechanical strength / adhesion of ice
rubrics_metrics.description: How to estimate the solidity of the body of ice, or how strong is the mutual adhesion of its parts; and whether differing degrees of cold vary the compactness of ice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use experiments to measure ice strength, compare ice formed under different coldness degrees, and supplement laboratory work with descriptive observational reports from cold-region travellers/seamen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate properties of sea-ice vs fresh-ice
rubrics_metrics.description: Record observations touching the insipidness (lack of taste) of resolved ice made of sea-water and the prodigious magnitude (height/length) of sea-ice as reported by seamen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare chemical/physical properties of sea-water ice and fresh-water ice, and correlate experimental findings with navigators' journals on ice size and behaviour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods for preserving ice and comparing dissolving rates
rubrics_metrics.description: How ice and snow may be made to last long; and what liquor dissolves ice sooner than others, and in what proportion of quickness the solutions in the several liquors are made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experiment with various substances and conditions to determine ice preservation techniques and relative dissolution rates; investigate whether motion imparts heat to ice (e.g., heating a cold liquor with ice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Apertures of object-glasses proportional to length
rubrics_metrics.description: The apertures which optic glasses can bear with distinctness are in about the subduplicate proportion of their lengths (Auzout's claim and table of apertures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design objective apertures following the approximate subduplicate (square-root) relation to telescope length; consult provided aperture table for 'excellent', 'good', 'ordinary' classifications at different lengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aperture prescription for planetary illumination experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: To enlighten an object in any proportion desired: for every nine feet draught, or thereabouts, one inch of aperture be given for the earth (used to compare planetary illuminations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select aperture scaled to presumed distance/illumination when simulating planetary lighting; use to compare relative light available for burning or observation across planets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility limits on making extremely long objective glasses
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical limit: making glasses of above 300 or 400 feet is feared impracticable as neither matter nor art may go so far (objection to Hook's turning-engine for very long lenses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognise material and technical limits when planning very large optics; consider that beyond a few hundred feet current methods may be infeasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observational consistency to test astronomical hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: Use repeated observations (e.g., appearances/shadows on Saturn's ring and disk, spots/shadows on Jupiter) at different aspects (trine, sextile, oriental, occidental) to assess whether features are shadows, prominences, or instrumental/artifact effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare observations across different geometrical configurations of planet and sun to test ring and satellite-shadow hypotheses; expect particular shadow placements if a ring exists and use discrepancies to question hypotheses or instrumentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design of mine ventilation without air-shafts
rubrics_metrics.description: A ventilation contrivance: a brick chimney (28–30 ft high) with a sealed ash-hole, a square hole fitted with a wooden tube carried into the adit, joints stopped with parchment, always lengthened as adit advances, and a fire kept burning to draw fresh air; use two iron grates in rotation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure airtight joints, maintain continuous fire to drive airflow, lengthen the air-pipe as necessary, provide redundancy in grates, and heighten the chimney to improve draft. This arrangement removes noxious vapours and supplies breathable air for miners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rock-breaking method using drilled hole and explosive wedge
rubrics_metrics.description: Make a 18–20 inch deep hole with a steeled iron piercer, fit a double wedge into the hole (two diagonal pieces making a cylinder), grease adjoining faces, place a cartridge of gunpowder in a groove in the upper wedge, prime and fire to drive wedges and crack rock.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use specified tool dimensions and angles adapted to rock hardness, rotate the piercer between hammer blows, clean chips, fit wedges exactly, provide priming and safety preparations (burning match/thread to allow retreat), and brace wedges to direct force; expect cracking and ejection of rock.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record and analyse tidal irregularities with lunar phase and season
rubrics_metrics.description: Observe and report extraordinary reciprocations of flux and reflux (tides) relative to lunar phases (quarter moons, full/new) and seasonal changes (equinoctial variation where day and night currents reverse seasonally).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect systematic local timing of flood/ebb directions and durations across lunar cycle and seasons; use eyewitness reports when direct observation is unavailable, and note persistence and repeatability of patterns.
